title: Going-to-the-Sun Road, Rim to Lake
summary: Sunrise at Logan Pass, then the full Going-to-the-Sun Road east to west, ending with dinner in Kalispell.
drive: West Glacier to Kalispell via Going-to-the-Sun Road · 5h · 180 km

segments.name: Segment 1 — Logan Pass at Sunrise and the East Side
segments.blurb: Sunrise from the road's high point; it can close for snow after mid-September.

stops.name: Logan Pass
stops.note: Highest point on Going-to-the-Sun Road, 6,646 ft.

stops.name: Hidden Lake Overlook
stops.q: Hidden Lake Overlook Glacier National Park
stops.note: Short boardwalk hike from the Logan Pass visitor center.

stops.name: Saint Mary Falls
stops.q: Saint Mary Falls Glacier National Park
stops.note: Trailhead waterfall on the east side.

stops.name: Sunrift Gorge
stops.note: Narrow rock gorge cut by Baring Creek.

stops.name: Sun Point Nature Trail
stops.q: Saint Mary Lake Glacier National Park
stops.note: Short trail with views across Saint Mary Lake.

stops.name: Wild Goose Island Lookout
stops.q: Wild Goose Island Glacier National Park
stops.note: Classic overlook of the small island in the lake.

stops.name: Explore Saint Mary
stops.note: Small gateway town at the east entrance.

expect.arrive: Sunrise at 6,646 ft is windy and often near freezing in late September; the visitor center doesn't open until 9am.
expect.parking: By Sept 30 the 235-space lot is first-come, first-served, no time limit or shuttle needed.

paths.do: Watch sunrise from the Logan Pass lot and boardwalk edge, no hike.
Walk the boardwalk to the overlook and back.

paths.opt: Full loop plus St Mary stops
paths.do: Hidden Lake Overlook, then drive down to Sun Point and St. Mary Falls.

alt: Wild Goose Island Saint Mary Lake
segments.seasonal: GTSR's alpine section through Logan Pass can close for snow anytime from early September; NPS says it's typically open through the third Monday of October (Oct 19, 2026), but closures as early as Sept 3 have occurred — check nps.gov/glac road status the week before.

segments.name: Segment 2 — West Side to Kalispell
segments.blurb: Cedar boardwalk and the park's largest lake, then dinner off the mountain.

stops.name: Trail of the Cedars
stops.q: Trail of the Cedars Glacier National Park
stops.note: Boardwalk loop through old-growth cedar and hemlock.

trail.from: Avalanche Creek / Trail of the Cedars trailhead

stops.name: Avalanche Lake
stops.note: Optional add-on hike above Avalanche Gorge.

stops.name: Lake McDonald
stops.note: Largest lake in the park, historic lodge on its shore.

expect.arrive: Trail of the Cedars boardwalk is right off the road; the Avalanche Lake trailhead shares the same lot.
expect.parking: Avalanche Creek lot is small and is consistently the first in the park to fill.

paths.do: Flat boardwalk loop through old-growth cedar, no elevation gain.
Continue past the cedars up to the lake and back.
Skip the hike, stop at the lodge and lakeshore instead.

alt: Trail of the Cedars Glacier National Park
